pillars.name: Unity Catalog Foundation
pillars.short: Governed catalogs, schemas, and tables in Unity Catalog.
best_practices: Grant access through groups, not individual users.
Standardize a catalog/schema naming convention (by domain + medallion layer).
Enable system tables so readiness and usage can be measured.
pillars.summary: Unity Catalog is the unified governance layer for data and AI — a three-level namespace with centralized access control, lineage, auditing, and discovery that everything above it inherits.

source_queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_schemas FROM (SELECT * FROM `pos_venda`.information_schema.schemata) AS _t WHERE schema_name <> 'information_schema'

SELECT COUNT(*) AS total, SUM(CASE WHEN table_type IN ('MANAGED','MANAGED_SHALLOW_CLONE') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS managed FROM (SELECT * FROM `pos_venda`.information_schema.tables) AS _t WHERE table_schema <> 'information_schema'
SELECT COUNT(*) AS non_uc FROM hive_metastore.information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema <> 'information_schema'

SELECT table_catalog AS catalog, table_schema AS schema, COUNT(*) AS tables, SUM(CASE WHEN table_type IN ('MANAGED','MANAGED_SHALLOW_CLONE') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS managed FROM (SELECT * FROM `pos_venda`.information_schema.tables) AS _t WHERE table_schema <> 'information_schema' GROUP BY table_catalog, table_schema ORDER BY tables DESC LIMIT 500

pillars.name: Metadata Richness
pillars.short: Comments and descriptions on tables and columns, plus tags.
best_practices: Target high comment coverage on gold tables/columns before standing up Genie.
Add synonyms / business terms users actually say.
Review AI-generated comments — don't ship them unedited.
pillars.summary: Table and column comments, descriptions, and governed tags. Genie maps natural-language questions to the right tables and columns using this metadata, so its quality strongly predicts answer accuracy.

pillars.name: Relationships & Modeling
pillars.short: Primary/foreign keys and a curated gold layer for analytics.
best_practices: Pre-join where it simplifies the model for business questions.
Ensure stable identifiers and a clean grain on fact tables.
pillars.summary: Declared primary/foreign-key relationships and a curated, query-ready gold layer (often pre-joined dimensional models). Declared keys let Genie infer correct join paths instead of guessing.

pillars.name: Metrics
pillars.short: Metric views — the governed metrics foundation that feeds the ontology.

signals.label: Commented
signals.detail: Share of metric views with a description

best_practices: Centralize KPI logic in metric views, not repeated across dashboards/queries.
Certify metrics and record an owner for each.
Add synonyms reflecting how the business actually speaks.
pillars.summary: Unity Catalog metric views define measures, dimensions, filters, and joins once, in governed YAML, and reuse them across Genie, dashboards, SQL, notebooks, and external BI. This is the central pillar of the semantic foundation that feeds Genie Ontology.

pillars.name: Genie Agents
pillars.short: Curated Genie Agents with instructions, example SQL, and benchmarks.
pillars.note: Genie usage can't be read — the assessing identity needs SELECT on system.access.audit.
best_practices: Prefer gold/semantic objects; give the agent a tight, well-described scope.
Maintain a benchmark question set to catch regressions as you tune.
Curate instructions/examples — an uncurated agent answers poorly.
pillars.summary: A Genie Agent is a curated room where business users ask questions in natural language. Curation — instructions, example/verified SQL, benchmark questions, and the tables/metric views in scope — is what makes answers accurate.

source_queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total, SUM(CASE WHEN active_30d = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS active_30d FROM ( SELECT request_params.space_id AS space_id, MAX(CASE WHEN lower(action_name) = 'trashspace' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS trashed, MAX(CASE WHEN event_date >= current_date() - INTERVAL 30 DAYS THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS active_30d FROM system.access.audit WHERE service_name = 'aibiGenie' AND request_params.space_id IS NOT NULL AND request_params.space_id <> 'new' AND event_date >= current_date() - INTERVAL 90 DAYS GROUP BY request_params.space_id ) WHERE trashed = 0

best_practices: Capability-aligned domains, each with one accountable steward.
Certify the canonical assets in each domain so trusted answers win.

Certify your most-accessed resources first — high-traffic tables are where certification most improves Genie/ontology accuracy (this app flags how many of your top-10 most-accessed resources are certified).
Start with 3–5 high-value domains rather than boiling the ocean.
Before the native feature, organize assets with a governed `domain` tag and an `owner`/`steward` tag — this app assesses both.
pillars.summary: Domains organize data and AI assets into business-aligned groups, giving agents scoped context plus stewardship and certification signals. Before the native Domains feature, the same structure can be expressed with a governed `domain` tag and an `owner`/`steward` tag.

source_queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT tag_value) AS distinct_domains, COUNT(*) AS assignments FROM (SELECT tag_value FROM (SELECT * FROM `pos_venda`.information_schema.table_tags) AS _t WHERE lower(tag_name) IN ('domain', 'data_domain', 'business_domain', 'subject_area', 'data_product') UNION ALL SELECT tag_value FROM (SELECT * FROM `pos_venda`.information_schema.schema_tags) AS _t WHERE lower(tag_name) IN ('domain', 'data_domain', 'business_domain', 'subject_area', 'data_product') )
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT * FROM `pos_venda`.information_schema.table_tags) AS _t WHERE lower(tag_name) IN ('owner', 'data_owner', 'steward', 'data_steward')

SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT concat_ws('.', catalog_name, schema_name, table_name)) FROM (SELECT * FROM `pos_venda`.information_schema.table_tags) AS _t WHERE lower(tag_name) IN ('system.certification_status', 'certification_status') AND lower(tag_value) = 'certified'
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT * FROM `pos_venda`.information_schema.tables) AS _t WHERE table_schema <> 'information_schema'
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT concat_ws('.', catalog_name, schema_name, table_name)) FROM (SELECT * FROM `pos_venda`.information_schema.table_tags) AS _t WHERE schema_name <> 'information_schema'

SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT concat_ws('.', catalog_name, schema_name, table_name)) FROM (SELECT * FROM `pos_venda`.information_schema.table_tags) AS _t WHERE lower(tag_name) IN ('domain', 'data_domain', 'business_domain', 'subject_area', 'data_product')

WITH top AS ( SELECT source_table_full_name AS name, COUNT(DISTINCT created_by) AS n FROM system.access.table_lineage WHERE source_table_full_name IS NOT NULL AND source_table_catalog NOT IN ('system','__databricks_internal','samples') AND source_table_schema <> 'information_schema' AND event_date >= current_date() - INTERVAL 90 DAYS GROUP BY source_table_full_name ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 10 ), cert AS ( SELECT concat_ws('.', catalog_name, schema_name, table_name) AS name FROM system.information_schema.table_tags WHERE lower(tag_name) IN ('system.certification_status','certification_status') AND lower(tag_value) = 'certified' ) SELECT t.name AS name, t.n AS accesses, CASE WHEN c.name IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS certified FROM top t LEFT JOIN cert c ON t.name = c.name ORDER BY t.n DESC

SELECT catalog_name AS catalog, schema_name AS schema, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN lower(tag_name) IN ('domain', 'data_domain', 'business_domain', 'subject_area', 'data_product') THEN concat_ws('.', catalog_name, schema_name, table_name) END) AS domain_tagged, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN lower(tag_name) IN ('owner', 'data_owner', 'steward', 'data_steward') THEN concat_ws('.', catalog_name, schema_name, table_name) END) AS stewarded, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN lower(tag_name) IN ('system.certification_status', 'certification_status') AND lower(tag_value) = 'certified' THEN concat_ws('.', catalog_name, schema_name, table_name) END) AS certified FROM (SELECT * FROM `pos_venda`.information_schema.table_tags) AS _t GROUP BY catalog_name, schema_name ORDER BY domain_tagged DESC LIMIT 500

pillars.name: Adoption & Activity
pillars.short: Active users, query activity, and lineage richness.
pillars.note: System tables (system.access / system.query) are not enabled or not granted to the app service principal (recommended for this workspace-wide signal) or your user account.
best_practices: Measure adoption with system tables — don't assume it.
Tie stewardship to roles, not heroics.
pillars.summary: Sustained value depends on people: active users querying in natural language, an executive sponsor, defined steward/owner roles, and a feedback loop that keeps semantics and Genie answers accurate over time.
